audience: Engineers building or debugging MCP servers and agent tooling who use Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Claude Code with custom MCP servers and have been burned by a tool call that silently misbehaved.
single_takeaway: mcpsnoop sits in the real client-server data path and shows the tool calls the official inspector structurally cannot see.
viewer_action: star the repo and run mcpsnoop demo to see the live stream with nothing to set up
desired_feeling: the unsettled recognition that your debugger has been lying to you, then relief that the honest one exists
references: Wireshark and tshark live packet capture, the creator's own stated analogy
charmbracelet Bubble Tea TUI texture, its real framework
investigative split editing: shown-version versus what-really-happened
mandatories: canvas #12161c, accent #1fb6ff, secondary accent teal #00a6a4, cool near-white ink, JetBrains Mono lowercase throughout, terminal beats use only documented commands and outputs verbatim, tag the creator (Semyon Usachev, @krlntn) at the close, CC BY music attribution if required
success_criteria: a viewer who has never heard of mcpsnoop can state the blind-spot idea after one watch, the money shot lands the slow-flagged real call visibly with no narration needed, and the story reads fully muted
